Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

summarize verb

also summarise, sum up, give a summary, run through briefly, in brief

classical

Cic. Att. 5.16.1: summātim tibi perscrīberem
Varr. R. 2 praef. 7: breviter ac summātim percurram (Lewis & Short)

summātim

adverb, with a verb of telling or writing (perscrībere, percurrere)

in summary, briefly, in outline

Latin summarizes with an adverb and a plain verb: summātim perscrībere, to write a summary; breviter ac summātim percurrere, to run through in brief. Cicero ends a letter summātim adhūc ad tē, that is the gist so far (Att. 15.4a.1).

Other words

  • perstringō, perstringere, perstrīnxī, perstrictum — touch on briefly, run over

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.201: perquam breviter perstringere atque attingere (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. summarize

    Its first senses are to bind tight and to graze, and of words also to censure (aliquem perstringere, Cic. Planc. 33), so it is clearest with breviter: breviter perstringere.

Examples

  • itaque subsēdī in ipsā viā, dum haec quae longiōrem dēsīderant ōrātiōnem summātim tibi perscrīberem

    so I sat down right there on the road to write you a summary of these things, which really need a longer accountCic. Att. 5.16.1

  • Dīc summātim: quid factum est?

    Sum it up for me: what happened?composed

SourcesLewis & Short: summatim · Lewis & Short: perstringo

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. summarize.

Cicero, ad Atticum 5.16.1 and 15.4a.1, checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
